Short notes / CRM style:
- Company: Tempo Forge Systems — real-time personalization for mobile ad surfaces, mixing ranking + short chat prompts in pipeline.
- Workload: 60ms median target, p95 target <= 200ms for full request (model call + routing); expected steady-state 250-400 QPS during peak campaigns.
- Priority: latency first, then cost. Very sensitive to tail latency spikes during bid windows.
- Interested in: batching heuristics that keep latency SLOs, KV/prefix caching to reduce repeated context recompute, and aggressive quantization (4-bit) to reduce cost per token.
- Asked specifically: can Redwood run perf benchmarks showing 1) no-batch vs small-batch (N=2,4) latency tradeoffs, 2) KV cache hit-rate benefit for repeated user prefixes, 3) 8-bit vs 4-bit quantized model latency + quality delta for reranking top-10.
- Quality tolerance: reranking must keep top-3 recall > 95% vs FP32 baseline on their eval set (will supply eval prompts).
- Data residency: user profiles stored in US only, but audit logs must be retained 12 months. KMS integration required for keys.
- Quote from CTO on call: "We can save 3–4x on token cost if latency holds — but we can't sacrifice tail spikes during auctions."
- Internal stakeholders: CTO (Priya Menon), Lead ML Engineer (Jonas Kim), Infra Head (Diego Alvarez).
- Procurement notes: wants a 30-day POC contract with optional conversion to 12-month dedicated commit. Needs a 'burst' clause for campaign spikes.
- Action items: SE to design POC bench harness + quantized model variants; Security to provide SOC2 + KMS integration doc; Sales to prepare fixed-monthly POC quote.
